answers.answer: Each player starts with 25 money, 1 active worker on the notepad and 3 inactive workers lying on the spaces below it, 8 Zoo cards (keep 4 and discard 4), and 2 Final Scoring cards. Put all five Action cards side I up; Animals goes in the leftmost slot (strength 1) and the other four are assigned randomly to the remaining slots. Starting Appeal is staggered by turn order: first player 0, second 1, third 2, fourth 3.
answers.evidence: Personal setup C3: 1 active worker and remaining 3 lying down; D: 25 money; E: draw 2 Final Scoring cards; F: draw 8, keep 4, discard 4; B: Animals under leftmost slot, others randomly; C1: Appeal 0/1/2/3 by turn order.

answers.answer: Setup places 4 face-up Base Conservation Project cards in a four-player game, and 3 in two- or three-player games. Only a two-player game blocks spaces: with six tokens of an unused color, block the left level on the left project, the middle level on the middle project, the right level on the right project, and all three spaces in the donation area's left column. Those covered spaces cannot be used by either player. Three- and four-player games have no such blocking. Reveal the six-card display after all players have chosen their initial hand cards.
answers.evidence: Setup 5b–5c specifies 4 cards for 4 players, otherwise 3, and the three project levels plus three donation spaces blocked only in a 2-player game; Setup G reveals the display after hand selection.

answers.answer: Using the card in slot 4, remove it, shift the cards that were in slots 1–3 one slot right, then place the used card in slot 1; the former slot-5 card stays in slot 5. Set strength before the action, including any X-tokens spent beforehand; each X-token adds +1 strength. X-tokens gained during the action cannot boost that same action, and you can hold at most 5. An effect marked “after finishing” resolves after the action is complete, including the card movement.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: shift all cards left of the empty slot right and put used card in slot 1; strength is set before performing the action; each X-token adds +1 and max holding is 5; “After finishing” effects follow action completion including card movement.

answers.answer: No. You may not take a regular action that plays zero animals or builds zero buildings. Instead, select an Action card and take exactly 1 X-token; move that card to slot 1 and shift intervening cards right. Its strength and upgrade state do not matter. You cannot take this action while holding 5 X-tokens.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure says doing nothing and playing zero animals/buildings are not legal; X-TOKEN action says take exactly 1, still move the selected card to slot 1, and cannot use it at 5 X-tokens.

answers.answer: When the Break token reaches the last space, ignore any additional movement beyond it and gain 1 X-token for reaching that space. Finish the current turn, then carry out the break. Afterward reset the Break token to the starting space for the player count and continue clockwise with the next player.
answers.evidence: Break track: reaching the last space calls a break after the current turn, awards 1 X-token, ignores additional steps, and resets after the break; break procedure says play continues clockwise with the next player.

answers.answer: Side I advances the Break token 2 spaces, then either draws from the deck according to its table (maximum 3, with any required discard) or, at strength 5+, snaps exactly 1 display card of choice regardless of reputation and without a deck draw. Side II also advances the Break token 2 spaces; it can draw from the deck and/or from display cards within reputation range in any order, following its table, or snap exactly 1 card at strength 3+ (higher strength does not improve a snap). Snapping on either side ignores reputation; the reputation restriction applies only to Side-II display draws. The display is replenished at the end of your turn after cards are taken. There is no in-turn hand limit; discard down to the hand limit during breaks.
answers.evidence: CARDS action: both sides advance Break 2; Side-I draw or strength-5 snap; Side-II deck/range draws and strength-3 snap; snap is one card regardless of reputation; display refill at turn end; hand limit checked during breaks.

answers.answer: Reputation range includes the display card in the folder matching your counter and all lower-numbered folders; folders 1–6 correspond to reputation 1, 2–3, 4–6, 7–9, 10–12, and 13–15. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action (Cards II). Above 15, the counter stays on 15 and each remaining reputation step gives 1 Appeal. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.
answers.evidence: Reputation spaces and rewards gives folder ranges and requires Cards II for reputation 10; at 15 further reputation yields 1 Appeal per remaining step; “You may not look through the discard pile.”

answers.answer: Build I builds exactly 1 building whose size is at most the action strength. Build II can build any number of different buildings, with total size at most the strength, but not two identical buildings in one action. Buildings cost 2 money per space. The first building must cover at least one border space; later buildings must touch an existing building by at least one edge. Build only on empty spaces, not beyond the map, over other buildings, or on water/rock; spaces with the restricted icon require Build II. Kiosks must be at least 3 spaces from every other kiosk. Each pavilion immediately and only once gives 1 Appeal.
answers.evidence: BUILD action: Side I exactly 1, Side II different buildings with total size ≤ strength; pay 2 money per space; placement rules cover first/later adjacency, empty spaces, water/rock and restricted spaces; kiosks at least 3 spaces apart; each pavilion gives 1 Appeal.

answers.answer: Build I permits standard enclosures (sizes 1–5), kiosks, pavilions, and one Petting Zoo per zoo. Build II additionally permits a Reptile House and a Large Bird Aviary; each player may have at most one of each special enclosure. The supply has four of each special enclosure. Build cannot create unique buildings; those enter play only through Sponsor cards. With Build II, covering every buildable map space except water and rock (by any effect) immediately gives 7 Appeal.
answers.evidence: BUILD table lists the buildings and minimum Build side, each special enclosure maximum one per zoo; the supply has four of each; unique buildings only via Sponsor cards; covering every space except water/rock gives 7 Appeal.

answers.answer: Yes. Bonuses gained earlier in an action, including money, cards, and newly activated workers, may be used for later steps of that action, resolving items one at a time; pay each item before receiving its own benefit. Placement bonuses are taken immediately before building the next building, while effects marked “after finishing” wait until the entire action is complete (and card movement is done). When effects are simultaneous, the player chooses their order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: earlier bonuses may be used for later steps; pay each item before its own benefits. Build II: placement bonuses before next building, “after finishing” bonuses after the whole action. Animals: simultaneous effects are resolved in chosen order.

answers.answer: To play an animal, meet all left-side conditions, pay its cost, and house it in a legal empty enclosure. A partner zoo on the animal's continent reduces cost by 3 money per continent icon, including each icon on a double-continent card. An animal in a standard enclosure needs one empty enclosure of at least its required size (except Petting Zoo animals, which can only use the Petting Zoo); flip the whole standard enclosure to its occupied side, normally for one animal. Petting Zoo animals go only in the Petting Zoo. Reptiles and some birds may instead use a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary, marking the indicated spaces with supply tokens; special enclosures are not flipped and must have enough free capacity. Required water/rock adjacency applies to the selected housing, including special housing; count distinct adjacent terrain hexes, not repeated edges to the same hex. Pay costs before effects that return money. Appeal and ordinary effects happen during the action; “after finishing” effects wait until the Animals action is complete, after the Animals card has moved. If multiple effects are simultaneous, choose their order.
answers.evidence: ANIMALS action steps specify conditions, payment, partner discount per continent icon, empty housing, exact adjacency counting and effects; the enclosure table states standard occupancy flips and special capacity is marked with tokens without flipping.

answers.answer: Animals II allows animals from display cards within reputation range as well as from hand; pay the display folder number as an additional cost. At strength 5+, you may first gain 1 reputation at the very beginning of the action, which raises range for that action. The display is not replenished until the turn ends. Animals whose conditions include the upgrade-required icon may be played with Animals II.
answers.evidence: Side II: may play from display within reputation range for the folder-number cost; at strength 5+ reputation increases first at the very beginning; display refill waits until turn ends; upgrade-required conditions are allowed.

answers.answer: When building a Reptile House or Large Bird Aviary with Build II, you may move all suitable animals that fit from standard enclosures into the new special enclosure, choosing separately for each animal. Mark the special enclosure's occupied capacity with player tokens; it is not flipped. The summary does not specify which standard enclosure becomes empty after a transfer, or any selection or fallback rule for choosing that enclosure, so those parts are unsupported.
answers.evidence: Build II says that building either special enclosure lets you immediately move all suitable animals that fit from standard enclosures, choosing separately for each. The animal housing table says special capacity is marked with player tokens and special enclosures are never flipped; no standard-enclosure transfer selection rule is stated.

answers.answer: The four Association task strengths are reputation 2, partner zoo 3, university 4, and conservation project work 5. Side I performs exactly one task; Side II can perform one or more different tasks whose total value is no more than action strength. Each task needs 1 active worker, or 2 if one of your workers is already on that task; if 3 of your workers are there, you cannot do it again until after the break. Other players' workers on that task do not matter. Side II still follows these worker requirements for each task.
answers.evidence: ASSOCIATION action lists task strengths and Side-I/II limits; it states the 1/2 worker requirement, inability to repeat with 3 workers until break, and that other players' workers do not matter.

answers.answer: Partner zoos and universities are taken from the available Association-board spaces and placed on the lowest empty matching space on your zoo map; any printed bonus is taken immediately. The board is replenished at breaks so each partner zoo/university is available exactly once, skipping those all players already have. A player may have partner zoos from different continents only, at most four; the third or fourth requires Association II. Universities cannot be duplicated. Universities grant their shown reputation when acquired and research icons; one university option gives hand limit 5, the only way to raise the normal hand limit of 3.
answers.evidence: Association task descriptions state tiles come from the Association board, go to the lowest available map space, bonuses/reputation are gained on acquisition, partner continent/maximum and Association II restrictions, and no duplicate universities; break procedure replenishes tiles. University tiles describe the hand-limit-5 option.

answers.answer: Conservation Project work can support a project already in play, or play a project card from hand and support it immediately; with Association II, a new project can also come from the display within reputation range for its folder-number cost. A support must meet an uncovered condition and place one player token from the left edge of your zoo map on that condition. A reward level is usable only if no player's token is on it, each level holds one token total, and you normally may support each project only once. Removing a map token activates its printed bonus immediately; take that bonus before or after the project reward. When a new project exceeds the player-count limit, discard the rightmost project and return tokens on it to their owners' supplies, not their zoo maps. The summary gives this overflow rule for projects, but does not describe any separate overflow rule for project-support tokens beyond returning tokens on a discarded project.
answers.evidence: Association conservation-project work states entry from hand/support immediately, support conditions and one-token/once limits, and token from left map edge; removed token activates bonus immediately. Side II permits display projects for folder cost. Excess projects discard rightmost and return its tokens to owners' supplies.

answers.answer: A release project requires the animal's printed standard-enclosure size to match the depicted size exactly, even if the animal could also live in a special enclosure. Discard the animal and lose only its printed Appeal and its icons; keep conservation, reputation, ability-generated Appeal, and effects already earned. To free the animal's housing, if it could live in a special enclosure first remove its indicated special-enclosure tokens if possible; otherwise flip a standard enclosure. For a standard enclosure, choose the smallest occupied one meeting all requirements; if none does, choose the smallest occupied one meeting size alone; if none meets size, flip none. The rule applies to flock animals too.
answers.evidence: Release into the wild: exact printed standard size; lose printed Appeal and icons but retain listed gains; remove special-enclosure tokens if possible, otherwise flip the smallest qualifying occupied standard enclosure with the stated fallback, or none if no enclosure meets size; applies to flock animals.

answers.answer: Sponsors I plays exactly one Sponsor from hand if action strength is at least its level and conditions are met. Sponsors II plays one or more cards if action strength +1 is at least the sum of their levels; they may come from hand or from within reputation range on the display, paying each display card's folder number. Resolve cards one after another, fully resolving each card's instant effects before the next, except “after finishing” effects. The display is replenished at turn end, and Sponsors II also permits upgrade-required conditions. If using the money option, Sponsors I advances the Break token by strength and pays that full amount even if fewer steps remain; Sponsors II doubles that money.
answers.evidence: SPONSORS action states Side-I one card/level threshold, Side-II sum-of-levels threshold (+1), hand/display and folder cost, sequential resolution, and money option paying strength money or twice that on Side II.

answers.answer: Break order: discard to hand limit (normally 3, or 5 with the relevant university); return Multiplier, Venom and Constriction tokens from Action cards; recall workers and replenish partner zoos/universities; discard display folders 1 and 2, shift cards down, and refill; take income; reset the Break token. Kiosk income is 1 money per adjacent unique building, special enclosure, occupied standard enclosure, or pavilion; empty standard enclosures do not count, but empty special enclosures do. Income includes appeal-based money and break-income icons. When multiple players take display cards during break income, resolve them clockwise from the break initiator (or first affected player clockwise from them), refilling the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.
answers.evidence: Break procedure lists all six steps, the normal/expanded hand limits, kiosk qualifying neighbors and empty-enclosure exceptions, and display-card ordering with a refill between affected players.

answers.answer: At 2 Conservation, choose to upgrade an Action card or activate an additional worker. At 5 and 8, take either 5 money or the bonus token by that space. The first time anyone reaches 10, all players discard one Final Scoring card; if no one reaches 10, all discard one before final scoring. Check the end at the end of your own turn or during a break when Appeal and Conservation are in the same scoring area or pass one another. Appeal gained during another player's turn does not trigger it until the end of your own turn or a break, unless another player triggers the end first. The triggering player finishes their turn and all other players get one final turn; if triggered during a break, everyone gets one final turn. A Final Scoring card can award at most 4 Conservation. Victory Points equal Appeal minus the lowest Appeal value in the scoring area containing your Conservation counter. Highest positive total wins; ties go to the player who supported the most projects, then tied players share the win.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory: conservation rewards at 2, 5, 8, 10; end trigger timing, delayed own-turn gains and final turns; final-scoring cap of 4; VP formula and project-support tiebreak/share rule.
